parts.zh: 佛罗里达州一名青少年和亚特兰大一名女性在周六的年度七英里大桥跑比赛中分别赢得男子组和女子组总冠军
M: 嗯……我不知道这是不是个好主意
W: 其实我不会一个人住
M: 你确定吗?大城市的房租很高
W: 我们已经把这些都做了预算
M: 那往返学校怎么办?听起来你每天要在路上浪费好几个小时
W: 到学校大约一小时
M: 这倒是真的。但我不明白既然费用一样
W: 原因有很多。我们会有厨房
M: 我还不确定好处是否大于坏处
W: 哦,对。我们小时候就有一套

questions.stem: What does the news report say about Vaclav Bursa and Joanna Stephens?
options: They are young teenagers from Atlanta.
They won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run.
They completed the race in less than 40 minutes.
They are both students at Marathon High School.
optionsZh: 他们是来自亚特兰大的青少年。
他们赢得了今年的7英里桥梁跑比赛。
他们在不到40分钟内完成了比赛。
他们都是Marathon高中的学生。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：They won this year's 7 Mile Bridge Run.（他们赢得了今年的7英里桥梁跑比赛。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the April contest?
options: It drew competitors from more than 40 countries.
It is watched live online by fans all over the world.
It closed the city of Big Pine Key to traffic for three hours.
It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.
optionsZh: 它吸引了来自40多个国家的参赛者。
它被全世界的粉丝在线观看直播。
它使Big Pine Key市封闭交通三小时。
它是美国东南部最受欢迎的跑步赛事之一。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It is one of the most popular running events in the southeastern U.S.（它是美国东南部最受欢迎的跑步赛事之一。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the news report about Tim Peake?
options: He was once a full-time ambassador.
He was soon to retire from the army.
He became an astronaut in 2015.
He used to be a helicopter pilot.
optionsZh: 他曾经是一名全职大使。
他即将从军队退役。
他在2015年成为一名宇航员。
他曾经是一名直升机飞行员。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：He used to be a helicopter pilot.（他曾经是一名直升机飞行员。）

questions.stem: What does Tim Peake say about his work with the European Space Agency?
options: It has been unbelievably exciting and rewarding.
It has been extraordinarily tough and demanding.
It has contributed a great deal to human flights to space.
It has given him exceptional privilege as an ambassador.
optionsZh: 令人难以置信地激动人心且有意义。
异常艰苦且要求严格。
对人类太空飞行做出了巨大贡献。
作为大使赋予了他特殊的荣誉。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：It has been unbelievably exciting and rewarding.（令人难以置信地激动人心且有意义。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the five cats seen in the Asda store?
options: They are known for their loyalty to their owners.
They are brought in by the store's customers.
They are regular visitors to the store.
They are pets kept by the store staff.
optionsZh: 它们以对主人的忠诚而闻名。
它们是由商店的顾客带进来的。
它们是商店的常客。
它们是商店员工饲养的宠物。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：They are regular visitors to the store.（它们是商店的常客。）

questions.stem: What did some customers think when they saw the first cat routinely appear in the store?
options: It might be a nuisance to the loyal shoppers.
It might have been abandoned by its owner.
It might be 12 months old.
It might have got lost.
optionsZh: 它可能会给忠实顾客带来麻烦。
它可能被主人遗弃了。
它可能有12个月大。
它可能迷路了。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It might have got lost.（它可能迷路了。）

questions.stem: What are customers asked not to do?
options: Feed the cats.
Remove any store signs.
Sit in the shop aisles.
Bring in pets with them.
optionsZh: 喂猫。
移除任何商店标识。
坐在商店过道里。
随身带宠物进来。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Feed the cats.（喂猫。）

questions.stem: What has the woman been thinking of doing next semester?
options: Sharing her room with friends.
Cutting down her living expenses.
Living off campus.
Moving to the city center.
optionsZh: 与朋友合住一个房间。
削减她的生活开支。
住在校外。
搬到市中心。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Living off campus.（住在校外。）

questions.stem: What does the man suggest the woman take into consideration?
options: The facilities available.
Various costs involved.
Changes in living conditions.
The distance to her home.
optionsZh: 可用的设施。
涉及的各种费用。
生活条件的变化。
到她家的距离。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Various costs involved.（涉及的各种费用。）

questions.stem: What does the woman say she did during high school?
options: Went through much trouble.
Commuted to save money.
Studied on the bus.
Lived on campus.
optionsZh: 经历了很多麻烦。
通勤以省钱。
在公交车上学习。
住在校园里。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Studied on the bus.（在公交车上学习。）

questions.stem: What does the man say he'll do at the end of the conversation?
options: Discuss the matter with the woman's mother.
Make a decision within a few days.
Try his best to persuade his wife.
Weigh the benefits against the disadvantages.
optionsZh: 与这位女士的母亲讨论这件事。
在几天内做出决定。
尽力说服他的妻子。
权衡利弊。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：Discuss the matter with the woman's mother.（与这位女士的母亲讨论这件事。）

questions.stem: What is the woman doing?
options: Interviewing the man.
Looking for Lawrence.
Choosing a present for her nephew.
Helping the man with his shopping.
optionsZh: 正在面试这位男士。
正在寻找Lawrence。
正在为她的侄子挑选礼物。
正在帮这位男士购物。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Choosing a present for her nephew.（正在为她的侄子挑选礼物。）

questions.stem: How does the man describe Bobo Man, the action figure?
options: Quite educational.
Incredibly popular.
Driven by batteries.
Obviously childish.
optionsZh: 相当有教育意义。
非常受欢迎。
由电池驱动。
明显很幼稚。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Incredibly popular.（非常受欢迎。）

questions.stem: What kind of game does the woman think would be good for Lawrence?
options: One he loves for helping exercise his mind.
One he can play together with his sister.
One he finds interesting and challenging.
One he can play either alone or in a group.
optionsZh: 一个他喜欢的有助于锻炼思维的游戏。
一个他可以和妹妹一起玩的游戏。
一个他觉得有趣且有挑战性的游戏。
一个他可以单独玩或集体玩的游戏。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：One he can play together with his sister.（一个他可以和妹妹一起玩的游戏。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the conversation about the game Battleships?
options: It has been enjoyed by kids for decades.
It always reminds people of times of war.
It has been played both indoors and outdoors.
It distinguishes itself as one of the oldest games.
optionsZh: 几十年来一直深受孩子们喜爱。
总是让人想起战争时期。
既可以在室内玩也可以在室外玩。
作为最古老的游戏之一而与众不同。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：It has been enjoyed by kids for decades.（几十年来一直深受孩子们喜爱。）

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about the paradox of choice?
options: A display of a variety of products increases consumers' interest.
Too many choices decrease one's desire to buy.
Fewer choices lead to lower customer satisfaction.
Customers given more choices are more likely to get confused.
optionsZh: 多种产品的陈列会增加消费者的兴趣。
过多的选择会降低购买欲望。
较少的选择会导致较低的顾客满意度。
给予顾客更多选择更有可能使其感到困惑。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：Too many choices decrease one's desire to buy.（过多的选择会降低购买欲望。）

questions.stem: What did the psychologists want to find out in their 2012 study about jams?
options: What kind of display results in more sales.
What kind of display creates more interest.
What kind of display attracts a greater crowd of customers.
What kind of display leads to greater customer satisfaction.
optionsZh: 什么样的陈列方式会带来更多销售额。
什么样的陈列方式会产生更多兴趣。
什么样的陈列方式会吸引更多顾客。
什么样的陈列方式会带来更高的顾客满意度。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：What kind of display results in more sales.（什么样的陈列方式会带来更多销售额。）

questions.stem: What is the finding of an extensive study published in 2015?
options: There are situations where customers buy nothing.
There are tricks to increase customer satisfaction.
There are ways to predict customer preferences.
There are rules that motivate customers to buy.
optionsZh: 存在顾客什么都不买的情况。
存在提高顾客满意度的技巧。
存在预测顾客偏好的方法。
存在激励顾客购买的规律。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：There are rules that motivate customers to buy.（存在激励顾客购买的规律。）

questions.stem: What do many Americans think of volunteering?
options: Stressful.
Burdensome.
Worthwhile.
Energy-boosting.
optionsZh: 有压力的。
繁重的。
值得的。
提升精力的。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：Worthwhile.（值得的。）

questions.stem: How could companies ensure both employees and employers benefit from volunteering?
options: By linking it with employees' salary.
By taking it as the New Year resolution.
By improving work schedules.
By making it part of the job.
optionsZh: 将其与员工的薪水挂钩。
将其作为新年决心。
改善工作日程安排。
使其成为工作的一部分。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：By making it part of the job.（使其成为工作的一部分。）

questions.stem: What did 75% of employees say about volunteering in a survey?
options: It was very important to their well-being.
It had taken little of their spare time.
It was an outlet for their personal fulfillment.
It helped improve their working environment.
optionsZh: 它对他们的幸福感非常重要。
它几乎没有占用他们的业余时间。
它是他们实现个人价值的途径。
它有助于改善他们的工作环境。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：It was very important to their well-being.（它对他们的幸福感非常重要。）

questions.stem: What do we learn about the UK's retail sector food waste?
options: It amounts to 2,000 tons daily.
It mostly comes from supermarkets.
It is estimated at 11% of the UK's total food supply.
It has a lot to do with independent luxury food suppliers.
optionsZh: 它每天达到2000吨。
它主要来自超市。
它估计占英国食品供应总量的11%。
它与独立的奢侈食品供应商有很大关系。
questions.explain: 正确答案 B：It mostly comes from supermarkets.（它主要来自超市。）

questions.stem: What does Sophie André's business do in London?
options: It rents bicycles to deliver food.
It sells sought-after coffee beans.
It delivers luxury hand-made food.
It recycles waste food from the city.
optionsZh: 它出租自行车来配送食品。
它销售抢手的咖啡豆。
它配送奢侈的手工制作食品。
它回收利用来自城市的废弃食品。
questions.explain: 正确答案 C：It delivers luxury hand-made food.（它配送奢侈的手工制作食品。）

questions.stem: In what way does Sophie André's business differ from many food waste projects?
options: It pays special attention to the size and shape of its products.
It tries to escape the constraints of the current food system.
It cooperates closely with local producers.
It aims to provide high-quality products.
optionsZh: 它特别关注其产品的大小和形状。
它试图摆脱当前食品系统的限制。
它与当地生产商密切合作。
它旨在提供高质量的产品。
questions.explain: 正确答案 D：It aims to provide high-quality products.（它旨在提供高质量的产品。）

questions.stem: Why will suppliers always have a certain amount of surplus?
options: To ensure a regular supply.
To maintain a unique menu.
To make up for the waste products.
To meet customers' urgent demand.
optionsZh: 为了确保有规律的供应。
为了保持独特的菜单。
为了弥补废弃产品。
为了满足顾客的紧急需求。
questions.explain: 正确答案 A：To ensure a regular supply.（为了确保有规律的供应。）

sections.title: 写作
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅰ · 30 分钟 · 120–180 词

items.prompt: Suppose your university is conducting a survey to collect students' opinions on the appropriate use of AI technology in assisting learning. You are now to write an essay to express your view. You will have 30 minutes for the task. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
items.rubric: CET 写作 15 分制：切题 3、表达 9、字数 3
items.sample:
In my view, AI technology, when used appropriately, is a valuable ally in learning rather than a shortcut that
replaces genuine effort. Since our university is surveying students on this issue, I would like to voice my
support for embracing AI in a sensible, balanced way.
There are solid reasons for this position. First, AI tools raise learning efficiency: a chatbot can explain a
confusing grammar point instantly, check my essay for mistakes, or gather background material that once took
hours in the library. Second, AI offers personalized tutoring, adjusting its explanations to my own pace and
weak spots. Admittedly, however, over-reliance is a real danger; if students let AI think for them, their own
analytical skills will gradually wither.
Therefore, the key lies in "appropriate" use. We should treat AI as an assistant that guides and inspires, not a
machine that hands us ready-made answers. Used within this boundary, AI can truly make learning smarter.

items.stem: Sir Alfred Hitchcock was an English movie director and producer. Famously {{1}} to as 'The Master of Suspense,' Hitchcock is one of the most influential filmmakers in the history of {{2}} . He was an extraordinary director who entertained his audience with {{3}} and gripping suspense movies. His fascination with crime began at an early age when he was {{4}} by his father who made him spend a few minutes inside a prison for his misconduct. Hence, his movies are {{5}} of the guilt and innocence of the wrongdoer and the victim. He had a gift for creating stories that consisted of deceit, robbery, murder, corruption, and other criminal {{6}} with incredible plot twists in the storyline. The principal characters in his movies were often ordinary people {{7}} in unwanted and unavoidable situations. He was {{8}} productive and his amazing body of work is considered fascinating by the critics. Most of his movies have {{9}} the test of time and are considered to be masterpieces. He is also remembered by other filmmakers, for he continues to inspire them to be passionate about their work. He is also {{10}} by people around the world for his entertaining and exciting stories.
options: caught
cinema
engaging
graphically
highly
incentive
instincts
offences
punished
referred
stood
symbolic
tuned
visually
worshipped

sections.title: 长篇阅读匹配
sections.instructions: 真题 Part Ⅲ Section B · 10 句匹配段落

paragraphs.text: Freshly juiced fruit has become a basic dietary item—especially for busy, health-conscious consumers who can save time on making (and perhaps even chewing) their food without missing out on nutrients. Fruit juice also has been linked to claims that it can help you both lose weight and stay healthy. All of which, of course, has made it highly profitable. The global fruit and vegetable juices market was valued at $154 billion in 2016 and is expected to grow.

But is juicing really as healthy as we think? Most foods containing fructose—a naturally occurring sugar found in all fruits and fruit juices—don't seem to have harmful effects as long as they're not contributing to excess daily calories. This is because the fibre found in whole fruits is intact, and the sugar is contained within the fruit's cells. It takes our digestive system a while to break these cells down and for fructose to enter the bloodstream.

But this is not the case with fruit juice. Unlike whole fruit, fruit juice has most of the fibre removed. This is why the fructose in fruit juices counts as 'free sugars'—which also include honey and the sugars added to foods. It's recommended by the World Health Organisation that adults have no more than 30g of added sugar, the equivalent of 150ml of fruit juice, per day. The problem is that, with the fibre removed, fruit juice's fructose is absorbed more quickly. Sudden increases in blood sugar cause the release of insulin(胰岛素) to bring it back down to a stable level. Over time, this mechanism can wear out, increasing the risk of developing type 2 diabetes. In 2013, researchers analysed the health data of 100,000 people collected between 1986 and 2009 and found that fruit juice consumption was linked with increased risk of type 2 diabetes. Another study found a relationship between fruit juice and type 2 diabetes after following the diets and diabetes status of more than 70,000 nurses over 18 years. The researchers explain that the possible reason for this may partly have been the lack of the other components found in whole fruit, like fibre.

Juices containing vegetables can provide more nutrients and less sugar than juices made up of just fruit—but they still lack valuable fibre. Diets high in fibre have been linked to a lower risk of developing heart disease, stroke, high blood pressure and diabetes, and it's recommended adults consume 30g per day.

Aside from the link to type 2 diabetes, many studies agree that fruit juice is harmful if it contributes to an excess in calories. In an analysis of 155 studies, John Sievenpiper, associate professor at the University of Toronto's Department of Nutritional Sciences, set out to understand if the associations between sugary soft drinks and health—including risk of diabetes and heart disease—were applicable to the food and drink we generally consume as part of a healthy diet. He compared studies looking into the effects of fructose-containing sugars with control diets free from or lower in these sugars. His aim? To isolate the effects of consuming too many calories from the effects of foods containing different sugars.

He found negative effects on blood sugar and insulin levels when food provided excess calories from sugars, including fruit juice. However, when the calories weren't in excess overall, there were some advantages to consuming whole fruit—and even fruit juice. Sievenpiper concludes that the recommended 150ml of fruit juice per day, which is an average serving, is reasonable. The paper concluded that foods containing fructose may have some small benefits for long-term blood sugar control when they don't lead to over-consumption of calories. But when they do lead to too many calories, they risk raising blood sugar and insulin levels.

So while we know that fruit juice can cause diabetes if it's part of a diet that has more calories overall, it's less clear how juice affects the long-term health of those who aren't overweight. But we have a higher risk of consuming more than the recommended daily number of calories (around 2,000 for women and 2,500 for men) on the days we drink juice, according to research. Numerous studies have shown that drinking fruit juice doesn't make us consume any less of other foods throughout the day.

As it is easy to consume large amounts of fruit juice quite quickly, extra calories are taken in. And extra calories can contribute to weight gain. One way we can improve the effects of fruit juice on our health is making sure we select ripe fruit to retain as much of its goodness as possible, according to Roger Clemens, professor of pharmaceutical(药物的) sciences at the University of Southern California.

Another reason for fruit juice's recent popularity is the argument that it can help to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body. However, "the whole concept of a juice diet helping to remove poisonous or harmful substances from the body is completely false," says Clemens. "We consume compounds every day that may be poisonous and our bodies do a wonderful job of removing and eliminating anything harmful from our bodies."

And juice isn't a cure-all for getting your nutrients, either. "There are a lot of nutrients contained in the parts of the fruits, such as in apple skins, that are excluded when you juice them," says Heather Ferris, a professor of medicine. "You end up with sugary water with some vitamins."

Plus, she adds, it's not an ideal way to reach the advised 'five a day'. "People try to get five servings of fruit and vegetables per day and don't realise this isn't just about getting vitamins," she says. "It's also about reducing the amount of grain carbs(碳水化合物) and protein and fats in our diet, and increasing fibre." So while fruit juice is better than no fruit at all, there are limits. It particularly comes with risks when we consume more than 150ml of free sugars per day, or when it puts us over our recommended calorie intake. It provides us with vitamins—but fruit juice is far from a quick fix.

items.passage: We all take a little extra effort to look nice for special occasions. But most of us have conflicting feelings about dressing up and feel guilty about taking the time to focus on clothes. Science now suggests the right dress may give ourselves the extra edge in our professional and personal lives. We hear sayings like "dress for the job you want; not the job you have". Most people don't really believe in them, but research into the impact of clothes on behavior now suggests that there may actually be a grain of truth in these sayings. Science says that the clothes we wear affect our behavior, our mood and even the way we interact with others because of the symbolic meaning that we assign to different types of clothing. We consider some clothes to be powerful, some to be fun, and so on. We even evaluate people whom we have just met based on their clothes. We also evaluate ourselves based on what we are wearing because of the way they make us feel. This means that the experience of wearing something affects our attitudes and our choice of behavior. There's a reason tailored jackets are associated with being 'dressed for success'. It seems that wearing formal office wear puts us in the right frame of mind to conduct business. Wearing power clothing makes us feel more confident and even increases hormones needed for displaying dominance. This in turn helps us become better negotiators and abstract thinkers. While a good suit works wonders for our performance in the boardroom, wearing formal wear isn't a great idea when we want to socialize. Studies have found that people tend to be less open and less able to relax when they wear formal clothes. On the other hand, a casual dress helps us become more friendly and creative. These findings support the idea of wearing business casuals on a Friday; since colleagues are most likely to take out time to socialize on the last work day of the week. I mean, who wants to hang out with people in their suits?

items.passage: With the rise of pop music, jazz, and electronic music, both opera and classical music started to fade away from the public eye. Some people are beginning to wonder whether opera and classical music are still relevant to the modern world of music. Granted, you will not typically see today's teenagers lending their ears to Bach anytime soon, but there are some major indicators that both opera and classical music are now still quite alive. The most major indicator of classical music's importance in society today is the fact that much of the popular music that is currently being produced uses similar beats, harmonies, and melodies(旋律) as those that were used in some of classical music's best works. Even so, it can be difficult for those who do not study music theory to see this as an indicator, since it is subtle and just shows the impact symphonic(交响乐的) orchestras have had on society's taste in music. A better example for the relevance of opera and classical music can be seen in the invention of the rock opera. Opera, in its simplest definition, is telling a story using music as its form. The art of telling a story using music has not faded in the least bit. In fact, sometimes actual orchestras are used for major parts of the opera itself. Some of the world's greatest hits have been parts of rock operas. Fans of classical music can also tell you that there are few types of music that are more expressive. So, it should come as no surprise to anyone that classical music pieces are still used as background music in modern movies. Symphonic orchestra compositions have also been created solely for the purpose of being included in major motion pictures. These are often very well received amongst mainstream music fans. Classical music and opera are the very foundation of what our modern music is based upon. Considering the huge impact they have had on our current society, it is without doubt that we can expect them to continue to remain important for centuries to come.

items.zh: 近年来中国东北地区正在大力开发冰雪资源。例如哈尔滨利用丰富的冰雪资源打造了极具地方特色的"冰雪大世界"让游客在欣赏冰雪之美的同时也能体验当地独特的民俗文化。如今曾令人畏惧的冰天雪地正吸引着四面八方的游客成为深受欢迎的旅游胜地。冰雪旅游业正为当地的经济发展做出越来越大的贡献。
items.reference: In recent years, Northeast China has been vigorously developing its ice and snow resources. For example, Harbin has built the Ice and Snow World with strong local characteristics by making full use of its rich ice and snow resources, allowing tourists to experience the unique local folk culture while enjoying the beauty of ice and snow. Today, the once-feared land of ice and snow is attracting tourists from all directions and has become a popular tourist destination Ice and snow tourism is making an increasingly great contribution to the local economic development.
